## Comparability caveat

All five companies report on a calendar fiscal year (Jan 1 – Dec 31, 2024), so there is no fiscal-year mismatch [DOC-1]. However, **Alaska Air Group's FY2024 is not organically comparable** to the prior year or to the other carriers: "On September 18, 2024, Alaska Air Group completed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings, Inc. … The results of Hawaiian are included in the consolidated financial statements beginning September 18, 2024. For the period from the acquisition date to December 31, 2024, revenue and net loss from Hawaiian recognized in the Company's consolidated results of operations was $869 million and $113 million, respectively" [DOC-2]. Alaska's FY2024 therefore blends ~12 months of legacy Alaska with ~3.5 months of Hawaiian, and the Hawaiian stub period was loss-making, depressing Alaska's margins.

## Operating margin (operating income ÷ revenue), FY2024

| Rank | Airline | Operating income | Revenue | Operating margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delta | $5,995M | $61,643M | **9.7%** [DOC-1] |
| 2 | United | $5,096M | $57,063M | **8.9%** [DOC-1] |
| 3 | Alaska | $570M | $11,735M | **4.86%** [DOC-1] |
| 4 | American | $2,614M | $54,211M | **4.82%** [DOC-1] |
| 5 | Southwest | $321M | $27,483M | **1.2%** [DOC-1] |

Note: the Alaska/American gap (4.86% vs. 4.82%) is essentially a tie and is sensitive to the Hawaiian consolidation noted above.

## Net margin (net income ÷ revenue), FY2024

| Rank | Airline | Net income | Revenue | Net margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delta | $3,457M | $61,643M | **5.6%** [DOC-1] |
| 2 | United | $3,149M | $57,063M | **5.5%** [DOC-1] |
| 3 | Alaska | $395M | $11,735M | **3.4%** [DOC-1] |
| 4 | Southwest | $465M | $27,483M | **1.7%** [DOC-1] |
| 5 | American | $846M | $54,211M | **1.6%** [DOC-1] |

Excluding the acquired Hawaiian operations, Alaska's implied net margin would be roughly ($395M + $113M) ÷ ($11,735M − $869M) ≈ 4.7% [DOC-1][DOC-2] — higher, but still third behind Delta and United.

## Conclusion

Yes — **Delta is top-ranked on both measures** (9.7% operating margin and 5.6% net margin), with United a close second in each case. The rankings differ only in the bottom two positions: American is fourth on operating margin but last on net margin, while Southwest swaps into fourth on net margin.

ANSWER: Operating margin: Delta 9.7% > United 8.9% > Alaska 4.86% > American 4.82% > Southwest 1.2%. Net margin: Delta 5.6% > United 5.5% > Alaska 3.4% > Southwest 1.7% > American 1.6%. Yes — Delta ranks first on both (note: Alaska's FY2024 includes only Sept 18–Dec 31 of acquired Hawaiian, $869M revenue and $113M net loss, so it is not a like-for-like comparison).
